chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Safwan, from Ibn Sinan; and Hammad, from Ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who performed tamattu' and did not find a sacrificial offering. He said: then let him fast three days, excluding the Days of Tashriq from them; rather, he should remain in Makkah until he fasts them, and seven when he returns to his family. And he mentioned the hadith of Budayl ibn Warqa'.

key_terms.أَيَّامُ التَّشْرِيقِ: the Days of Tashriq, which are excluded here
key_terms.بِمَكَّةَ: in Makkah, where he must remain to complete the fast
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: three days of fasting as a substitute
key_terms.سَبْعَةً: seven additional days of fasting after returning
key_terms.هَدْيًا: a sacrificial offering required in this pilgrimage context

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim performing tamattu' do if he cannot find a sacrificial offering?
ai.summary: This hadith gives the legal ruling for one performing hajj al-tamattu' who cannot find or provide the sacrificial offering. He must fast three days in Makkah, not including the Days of Tashriq, and then fast seven more days after returning to his family.
